questions.prompt:
Two Cisco IOS switches connect through an operational 802.1Q trunk. Two PCs should communicate directly within VLAN 20:

```text
PC-A -- SW1 Fa0/1 [VLAN 20] -- SW1 Gi0/1 === SW2 Gi0/1 -- SW2 Fa0/1 [VLAN 20] -- PC-B
PC-A: 192.0.2.10/24                                            PC-B: 192.0.2.20/24
```

Both access ports are up and correctly assigned to VLAN 20. VLANs 10, 20, and 30 exist and are active on both switches. Spanning Tree permits forwarding for these VLANs, and neither switch has an ACL or port-security restriction. The relevant output is:

```text
SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port   Mode  Encapsulation  Status    Native vlan
Gi0/1  on    802.1q         trunking  1
Port   Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1  10,30

SW2# show interfaces trunk
Port   Mode  Encapsulation  Status    Native vlan
Gi0/1  on    802.1q         trunking  1
Port   Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1  10,20,30
```

Which command, entered under `interface Gi0/1` on SW1, corrects this fault while preserving trunk carriage of VLANs 10 and 30? Select one.

distractor_explanations.B: Changing the native VLAN does not add VLAN 20 to the allowed list and would also introduce a native-VLAN mismatch.

|---|---|---|

questions.topic: Spanning Tree root and root-port selection
questions.prompt:
Four Cisco switches run one stable PVST+ instance for VLAN 20. The table shows their configured base priorities and MAC addresses. Each bridge ID also contains the same VLAN 20 system-ID extension.

| Switch | Base priority | MAC address |
|---|---:|---|
| SW1 | 24576 | 00ff.0000.0001 |
| SW2 | 32768 | 0022.0000.0002 |
| SW3 | 32768 | 0011.0000.0003 |
| SW4 | 28672 | 0001.0000.0004 |

The only links are shown below. Every port has an explicitly configured STP cost of 4. Port priorities are all equal, and no protection feature changes normal STP selection.

```text
             SW1
            /   \
          SW2   SW3
            \   /
             SW4

SW4 Gi0/1 connects to SW2.
SW4 Gi0/2 connects to SW3.
```

After convergence, which combination identifies the root bridge and SW4's root port? Select one.

options.A: Root bridge: SW1; SW4 root port: Gi0/1
options.B: Root bridge: SW1; SW4 root port: Gi0/2
options.C: Root bridge: SW4; SW4 root port: Gi0/1
options.D: Root bridge: SW3; SW4 root port: Gi0/2

questions.explanation: SW1 has the lowest bridge priority, so it is root despite its higher MAC address. SW4 has an equal root-path cost of 4 + 4 = 8 through SW2 and SW3. The next relevant tiebreaker is the upstream sender's bridge ID. SW2 and SW3 have equal priorities, but SW3's MAC address is lower; SW4 therefore selects Gi0/2 toward SW3.

distractor_explanations.A: The root is correct, but the equal-cost comparison prefers SW3's lower bridge ID. SW4's lower local port number is not the deciding factor.
distractor_explanations.C: SW4's lower MAC does not overcome SW1's lower priority. A root bridge also does not select a root port for its own instance.
distractor_explanations.D: SW3's priority is higher than SW1's; its lower MAC matters only after equal priority.

sources: Study Notes/25 STP - Spanning Tree Protocol/25-05 How Spanning Tree Works.pdf
source_sections: The Bridge ID; The Root Bridge; Spanning Tree Path Cost; Root Ports; Load Balancing
questions.verification: Independently reviewed before exam start; source text inspected.

questions.prompt:
A Cisco IOS switch uses this configuration on a port intended for one desktop:

```text
interface FastEthernet0/10
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 30
 spanning-tree portfast
 spanning-tree bpduguard enable
```

Someone connects an unmanaged Ethernet switch that sends BPDUs. The Cisco switch reports:

```text
%PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: bpduguard error detected on Fa0/10, putting Fa0/10 in err-disable state

SW1# show interfaces status
Port    Status        Vlan
Fa0/10  err-disabled  30
```

Automatic errdisable recovery is disabled. The required policy is to retain PortFast and BPDU Guard on this desktop port. Which action restores the intended service and preserves that policy? Select one.

options.A: Leave the added switch connected and enable automatic recovery every 30 seconds.
options.B: Remove the added switch, reconnect the intended desktop, then issue shutdown followed by no shutdown on Fa0/10.
options.C: Leave the added switch connected and remove spanning-tree bpduguard enable.
options.D: Issue spanning-tree portfast again and wait; the port will automatically recover.

questions.explanation: BPDU Guard error-disabled the port after a BPDU arrived. Remove the cause first, then administratively shut and reenable the interface to recover it. The existing PortFast and BPDU Guard commands remain in place, preserving the intended desktop-port policy.

distractor_explanations.A: This leaves the cause present and can repeatedly restore and disable the port; it does not restore the intended desktop-only service.
distractor_explanations.C: This removes the required protection and leaves the unapproved device connected.
distractor_explanations.D: Reapplying PortFast does not clear an errdisabled state. Automatic recovery is explicitly disabled.


The server has an active scope for 10.30.0.0/24 with the correct gateway. A client using a temporary static address can ping the server. ACLs and DHCP snooping are absent. R1 is not a DHCP server. The clients send DHCPDISCOVER broadcasts but receive no offers. R1 has no helper addresses configured.

Which change enables R1 to relay these clients' requests to the server? Select one.

options.A: Under R1 Gi0/1, configure ip helper-address 10.40.0.20.
options.B: Under R1 Gi0/0, configure ip helper-address 10.40.0.20.
options.C: Under R1 Gi0/0, configure ip address dhcp.
options.D: Under R1 Gi0/1, configure ip helper-address 10.30.0.1.

questions.explanation: The router does not normally forward the clients' local broadcasts between subnets. Configure ip helper-address 10.40.0.20 on Gi0/0, the interface receiving the client broadcasts. The helper targets the DHCP server, which already has the correct scope and IP reachability.

distractor_explanations.A: Gi0/1 faces the server, so this would not relay client broadcasts arriving on Gi0/0.
distractor_explanations.C: ip address dhcp makes the router interface a DHCP client; it does not relay LAN clients' requests and would replace the intended static addressing behavior.
distractor_explanations.D: This uses the wrong receiving interface and targets the client gateway rather than the DHCP server.

questions.prompt:
A Cisco IOS edge router uses inside-source PAT. Its active TCP translations include:

```text
R1# show ip nat translations
Pro Inside global          Inside local          Outside local       Outside global
tcp 198.51.100.14:40001     10.24.6.11:51000       203.0.113.80:443     203.0.113.80:443
tcp 198.51.100.14:40002     10.24.6.12:51000       203.0.113.80:443     203.0.113.80:443
```

A return TCP packet arrives from 203.0.113.80, source port 443, addressed to 198.51.100.14, destination port 40002. Assume the displayed translations are still active and routing and ACLs permit delivery. After NAT, what are the packet's destination IP address and destination TCP port? Select one.
questions.explanation: The return packet matches the second translation's TCP outside endpoint and inside-global address/port. R1 restores the destination to the corresponding inside-local tuple, 10.24.6.12:51000. PAT distinguishes the two hosts using different translated port numbers even though they used the same original source port.

distractor_explanations.B: 40002 is the translated global port; the active entry restores the inside-local port 51000.
distractor_explanations.C: 198.51.100.14 is the shared global address, not the inside host's destination address after translation.

questions.prompt:
This is a text-based Cisco IOS configuration simulation; no commands will run on a device. Start in global configuration mode.

```text
Office LAN                 R1                         ISP
10.42.8.0/24 -- Gi0/0 10.42.8.1/24
                         Gi0/1 [IPv4 address from ISP DHCP] -- ISP
```

Both interfaces are up. Their IP addressing, the default route, and return routing already work. Gi0/1 already uses ip address dhcp, and its address can change. There is no NAT configuration and no ACL 17. Assume classic IOS inside/outside NAT with overload support.

Configure R1 so that hosts in 10.42.8.0/24 share Gi0/1's current address for outbound connections, and new outbound connections continue to use that interface address after a DHCP address change. Use standard ACL 17 to identify exactly that /24. Include both interface NAT roles and the NAT rule. Do not change addressing or routing, and do not apply ACL 17 as an interface packet filter. Reply with IOS commands; exit and end are optional where the configuration context is otherwise clear.
questions.correct_answer:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip nat inside
exit
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip nat outside
exit
access-list 17 permit 10.42.8.0 0.0.0.255
ip nat inside source list 17 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload

all_required: Gi0/0 is designated ip nat inside
Gi0/1 is designated ip nat outside
Standard ACL 17 permits exactly 10.42.8.0/24 for NAT selection
An inside-source NAT rule references ACL 17 and the current address of Gi0/1 with overload
No commands violate the stated constraints or undo required outcomes
equivalents: Accept valid IOS command abbreviations and interface abbreviations
Accept ip access-list standard 17 with equivalent permit entries
Accept a different command order if contexts and final outcomes are correct
An explicit deny any after the ACL permit is equivalent to the implicit deny
not_required: DHCP interface addressing or routing commands, which are already configured

questions.explanation: The LAN-facing interface is inside and the ISP-facing interface is outside. ACL 17 selects the office /24. The interface overload rule multiplexes connections onto Gi0/1's current address; using the interface reference accommodates address changes. A fixed global address or ordinary dynamic NAT without overload would not satisfy the requirements.

questions.prompt:
Assume a Cisco IOS Layer 2 switch with port security supported on this static access port. The abbreviated output is:

```text
SW1# show port-security interface FastEthernet0/6
Port Security              : Enabled
Port Status                : Secure-up
Violation Mode             : Restrict
Maximum MAC Addresses      : 2
Total MAC Addresses        : 2
Security Violation Count   : 3
```

The two allowed source MAC addresses are still present. A third, unauthorized source MAC sends frames into the port while an allowed host also transmits. No other security feature is involved, and normal switching permits the allowed host's traffic. What does the configured violation mode cause? Select exactly TWO.

options.A: Frames from the unauthorized source are dropped, and violations are logged and counted.
options.B: The port enters the error-disabled state and blocks both allowed and unauthorized sources.
options.C: The third source is automatically added as another permitted secure MAC address.
options.D: Frames from the already allowed sources continue to be forwarded.
options.E: The configured maximum automatically increases from two to three.

questions.explanation: Restrict drops unauthorized-source frames, logs violations, and increments the violation counter while continuing to forward permitted-source traffic. The displayed maximum remains two. The observed count does not imply the port has been shut down.

distractor_explanations.B: Error-disabling the entire interface is shutdown mode behavior, not restrict mode behavior.
distractor_explanations.C: The configured maximum is already reached; the unauthorized third source is not automatically accepted.
distractor_explanations.E: Violations do not increase the configured maximum.

questions.prompt:
An IOS router applies the following IPv4 ACL outbound on Gi0/1:

```text
ip access-list extended OFFICE_OUT
 10 permit tcp 10.14.0.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.90.0.20 eq 80
 20 deny ip host 10.14.0.25 any
 30 permit ip any any
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip access-group OFFICE_OUT out
```

The router is forwarding a TCP packet from 10.14.0.25, source port 49160, to 10.90.0.20, destination port 80, out Gi0/1. It originated on a LAN host, not on the router. Routing is valid and no other filter applies. What happens at this ACL? Select one.

options.A: It is denied by sequence 20 because the host-specific source overrides a subnet permit.
options.B: It is permitted by sequence 10, and no later entry is evaluated for this packet.
options.C: It is permitted by sequence 30 after all entries are evaluated.
options.D: It is denied by the implicit deny because its source TCP port is not 80.

questions.explanation: Sequence 10 matches TCP, source 10.14.0.25 within the permitted /24, destination 10.90.0.20, and destination port 80. IOS stops at that first match. ACLs do not choose the most specific entry the way a routing table chooses the longest matching prefix.

distractor_explanations.A: A later host-specific deny does not override an earlier matching permit.
distractor_explanations.C: Processing stops at sequence 10; sequence 30 is not reached.
distractor_explanations.D: The eq 80 after the destination address tests destination port 80. The source port is unrestricted by this entry.

questions.prompt:
This is a text-based Cisco IOS configuration simulation; no commands will run on a device. Start in global configuration mode.

```text
Workstation LAN                  R1                    Server LAN
10.12.30.0/24 -- Gi0/0 10.12.30.1/24
                             Gi0/1 10.50.0.1/24 -- server 10.50.0.20
Admin workstation: 10.12.30.10
```

Interfaces, routes, and host gateways already work. No ACLs are configured. Assume classic IOS IPv4 extended ACL support. Configure a named extended ACL called STAFF_FILTER and apply it inbound on Gi0/0 to implement all of these requirements:

- Permit TCP traffic from 10.12.30.10 to server 10.50.0.20, destination port 22.
- Deny TCP traffic from every other source entering Gi0/0 to that same server and destination port.
- Permit all other transit IPv4 traffic entering Gi0/0.

This policy filters forwarded traffic; it does not configure the router's own SSH service. Reply with the ACL entries and interface application commands. Valid equivalent IOS syntax is accepted; exit and end are optional where the configuration context is otherwise clear.
questions.correct_answer:
ip access-list extended STAFF_FILTER
 permit tcp host 10.12.30.10 host 10.50.0.20 eq 22
 deny tcp any host 10.50.0.20 eq 22
 permit ip any any
exit
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip access-group STAFF_FILTER in

all_required: Create named extended IPv4 ACL STAFF_FILTER
Permit 10.12.30.10 TCP traffic to 10.50.0.20 destination port 22
Deny all other sources to that TCP destination service
Permit every other transit IPv4 packet entering Gi0/0
Rule ordering and any extra commands preserve every required outcome
equivalents: Accept the IOS service keyword ssh for port 22 where supported under the stated IOS assumption
Accept optional sequence numbers and equivalent ordered entries
Accept different valid rule structures that satisfy the full policy for all possible IPv4 source addresses
not_required: VTY, RSA, username, interface addressing or routing configuration

questions.explanation: The administrator's TCP/22 exception must match before the general deny for that server's TCP/22 service. The final permit ip any any preserves unrelated IPv4 traffic that the implicit deny would otherwise block. Applying the ACL inbound on Gi0/0 filters packets as they enter from the workstation LAN. A deny limited only to the displayed /24 does not implement the stated every-other-source requirement for all packets entering that interface.

questions.prompt:
A network uses the controller architecture shown below. A business application sends policy requests to the controller over REST. The controller sends configuration to the infrastructure switches over NETCONF. The switches forward user packets.

```text
Business application
        |
        | REST policy requests
        |
  SDN controller
        |
        | NETCONF configuration
        |
Infrastructure switches
```

Which **two** statements correctly describe this architecture? Select **exactly two** answers.

options.A: The REST connection between the application and controller uses a northbound API.
options.B: The NETCONF connection between the controller and switches uses a northbound API.
options.C: The switches perform the management-plane function when they forward user packets.
options.D: The NETCONF connection between the controller and switches uses a southbound API.
options.E: The REST connection is classified as southbound because the application sends requests downward in the diagram.

questions.explanation: In the three-layer SDN architecture, northbound APIs connect the application layer to the controller layer, while southbound APIs connect the controller layer to the infrastructure layer. The direction in which an individual message travels does not rename the API. Forwarding user traffic is a data-plane function.

distractor_explanations.B: Controller-to-infrastructure communication uses the southbound API in this architecture.
distractor_explanations.C: Forwarding user packets belongs to the data plane. The management plane is used to configure and monitor devices.
distractor_explanations.E: The API classification follows the layers it connects, not the direction of an individual request or the way a diagram is drawn.
